results.quote: There is a deterministic algorithm that solves the induced subgraph connected component problem in time $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\mathrm{MM}(|\mathcal{S}|,n,n))$ for an n-node input graph and a non-empty input set S.

results.problem: Neighborhood-deleted components, extremities, star cut-set, fixed two-pair
results.quote: The following problems have a deterministic $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^\omega)$-time algorithm on an n-node input graph: computing neighborhood-deleted components in a graph, listing all extremities in a graph and determining whether the graph has a star cut-set, determining whether two fixed vertices x, y are a two-pair.
There is a deterministic $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^\omega)$-time algorithm that determines if a graph is AT-free.
There is a deterministic $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^\omega)$-time algorithm for listing all dominating pairs.
There is a deterministic $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^\omega)$-time algorithm for listing all two-pairs.
There is an algorithm for Decremental Simplicial Vertex that on an n-node graph runs in time $\mathcal{O}\left(min_{\Delta\in[1..n]}\left\{n/\Delta\cdot MM(n,\Delta,n)+m\cdot\Delta\right\}\right)$.

results.bound: Triangle detection reduces to uv-trail detection in O(T) time
results.quote: For any $k\ge 3$, suppose there exists an algorithm that, in time $\mathsf{T}=\Omega(n^2)$, determines whether an n-node graph $\mathbf{G}$ contains a uv-trail for two vertices u,v with d(u,v)=k. Then there is an algorithm solving triangle detection in time O(T).
